extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is a vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans, covering 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes. It is designed to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first collected from existing benchmarks, then filtered using an automated pipeline with LLM inspectors to remove visually unnecessary or leaked samples, followed by manual review by three experts to curate 1,500 high-quality samples covering various capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples drawn from six existing benchmarks: two focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge, totaling 22,401 samples before filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: 1) each sample's answer is based on visual content understanding; 2) selected samples cover comprehensive capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples require advanced multi-modal abilities. Samples were split into four difficulty categories (easy, moderate, hard, tough) based on hit counts from 16 LVLMs, and 1,500 high-quality samples were manually curated from the coarsely filtered set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Automated coarse filtering using LLM inspectors (2 closed-source and 6 open-source LLMs) to check visual dependency and data leakage; samples retained only if hit count was two or fewer (i.e., ~75% of LLM inspectors failed to answer correctly). Sample pool reduced from 22,401 to 11,607 after filtering.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs (sizing 20B or larger) used as automated inspectors for coarse filtering; open-source LLMs applied with 2-shot in-context inference strategy.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Many samples in existing multi-modal benchmarks lack visual dependency or have been leaked into LLM/LVLM training data, leading to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance. The MMStar benchmark itself is limited to 1,500 samples and may not cover all capability dimensions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to provide more accurate evaluation of large vision-language models, which could guide the development of more capable and reliable AI systems. Inaccurate benchmarks could misguide research directions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The MMStar benchmark is intended for evaluating (testing) large vision-language models (LVLMs) on their actual multi-modal capabilities across 6 core capability dimensions and 18 detailed axes, using accuracy, multi-modal gain (MG), and multi-modal leakage (ML) metrics.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples were filtered using automated LLM-based inspection, split into difficulty categories (easy, moderate, hard, tough), and manually curated to ensure diversity across capability dimensions and difficulty levels, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 1,500 samples. Each core capability was balanced to contain 250 samples with relatively even distribution across 18 detailed axes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline was developed to filter samples based on visual dependency and minimal data leakage criteria. Two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs (20B+) were used as inspectors with 2-shot in-context inference to evaluate samples, retaining only those with two or fewer correct answers from the LLM inspectors. Three human experts then conducted manual review to verify visual dependency, capability coverage, and difficulty requirements.

name.evidence: we present MMStar, an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans.

description.evidence: MMStar is a premier, vision-critical multi-modal benchmark that includes 1,500 challenging samples, each rigorously validated by humans. It is structured to test 6 fundamental capabilities and 18 specific dimensions, aiming to evaluate the multi-modal capacities of LVLMs with a carefully balanced and purified selection of samples.
